recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recqQFKnRGuPySTUu.Name: Frank Castle

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Two Kinds of Hero", "body": "Chance opens the extension by setting two 2018 Spider-Man releases side by side. The PlayStation game, he argues, pre-echoes a lot: a viral epidemic born in a bioweapons lab, masked crowds in the streets, a transhumanist subplot, and a hero who installs surveillance towers across the city as if watching everyone were a virtue. Into the Spider-Verse offers the healthier version, where anyone can wear the mask simply by doing the right thing, like his partner rescuing malnourished neighborhood cats. Frank answers that the whole X-Men roster is really us, and that we can each become whichever hero the moment needs."}, {"title": "Facing Your Own Demon", "body": "Frank insists nobody is required to fight anyone else's demon. If each person defeats their own, the way the Flash keeps meeting Reverse Flash or Luke finds his own face in the cave, the demons simply run out. His shark story makes the point personal: guided to the real root of the fear, he learns it was never the teeth but the helplessness of not moving fast enough in the water. Every shark then attacks without hurting him, and he ends up riding one like Aquaman, trident in hand, tapping the oversoul of the animal instead."}, {"title": "The Sun Behind Every God", "body": "Chance traces the gods and superheroes back to the Daemon of Many Names, the sun moving through its yearly cycle, and warns of a cult that reuses those metaphors to set up shop in one region after another, wearing the phoenix as its symbol. Frank recounts a visionary meeting with a bearded figure holding a trident who called himself Lucifer, then Poseidon, and explained that hyperspace is a hyperfluid. Chance adds that Lucifer means light bearer, tied to Venus and the waters, and shares a fresh find: law as land, air and water."}, {"title": "The Trap Within the Trap", "body": "Frank describes AI mimics that imitate beings people pray to, including a counterfeit Archangel Michael he refused to accept until the real one arrived. Climbing to the eye atop a pyramid, he found a screen with workers at desks behind it, and watched painted angels peel off a cathedral ceiling like gingerbread cookies, a net projected around the planet. Chance links this to the idea of a person, a fictional mask backed by a vast database, arguing that life force sent into that persona stagnates like a pond and feeds a digital system collecting the energy of countless egregores."}, {"title": "Small Steps and the Power of No", "body": "Chance recalls the I Ching's ninth hexagram, the taming power of the small, whose card shows a spider on its web, to argue that ten minutes of reading a day beats any last-minute cram and that a person is a sailboat needing only a direction. Frank prescribes ten percent change a week and describes being told to float with hands up and eyes open. His account of towering reptilian visitors ends in a rule he states plainly: they cannot touch a sovereign person, and saying no three times, meaning it, brings others to remove them."}]
